svg.text: nano-rope against text-rope, yi-rope and core-text
A run is 10,000 operations on 100,000 lines of source code (4.0 MB), or one load or save of it. GHC 9.14.1, chunks scanned with AVX2.

svg.text: Fresh: a freshly loaded rope. Edited: the same rope after 10,000 random inserts, in the shape it has mid-session. Rows
with one run are on a fresh rope.
A freshly loaded text-rope or core-text is a single chunk, and core-text is the Text it was loaded from, so loading
and saving them is far faster than nano-rope; their first reads and splits walk the whole text.
No mark: the library cannot do this (yi-rope has no UTF-16, core-text neither UTF-16 nor lines). A hollow mark at the
right: left out, a run takes minutes.
Live heap: what stays reachable after a major collection once the Text the document came from is dropped. A rope that
shares that Text keeps it alive.
